memory_candidates.content: When reviewing a markdown-only governance/design record in this repo (records/*.md), checking it against records/README.md's 'which decisions are open' requirement is mechanically checkable: grep the candidate record and its siblings for case-insensitive 'alternative|reject' occurrence counts. A record with zero hits while its siblings each have several is a concrete, citable idiom gap (missing '## Open decisions' / no stated rejected alternatives), not a subjective style complaint.

In BimodalLogic, a PR whose branch name/number suggests it is late in a stack (e.g. '[3/3]') will show a diff against main that is the cumulative content of every earlier branch in the stack, not just its own unique work. Before inventorying 'what's unique to this PR', diff its file list (gh pr view --json files) against the file lists of the PRs it is presumably stacked on; content appearing in an earlier, still-open sibling PR is very likely superseded there (in a cleaned-up form) rather than uniquely owned by the later PR.

FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/README.md in BimodalLogic directly states the decidability ceiling: the tableau's full decidability biconditional is retired as vacuous; the only landed decidability result is decidableValidZTime (ZTime only, Formula only i.e. no stability operator, empty premises, via a presentation-free witness-family certificate); IntPresentation.lean gives the one genuinely finite model presentation (Fin-card ZTime frame) but only decides satisfiability of that presented frame, not the logic. Cite this README directly for any 'what would a decision procedure over these models need' question instead of re-deriving it from the tableau code.
